title: Circle theorems
cover_sub: Seven theorems, and a reason for every angle. Secure spotting each theorem, extend to tangents and isosceles triangles hiding in radii, then master multi-step chains and proof.

levels_long.s: One theorem at a time, with the reason written.
levels_long.e: Tangents from a point, radii, the alternate segment, algebra, and tampered evidence.
levels_long.m: Chains of theorems, proofs, and chords.

briefing: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference. The angle in a semicircle is 90°. Angles in the same segment are equal. Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°.

A tangent meets a radius at 90°. Two tangents from one point are equal. The angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment. The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects it. Two radii make an isosceles triangle.
method: Mark every radius: two radii mean an isosceles triangle.
Look for the shape the theorem needs: a 'bow tie', an 'arrowhead', a quadrilateral, a tangent.
Write the angle and the theorem's reason, every time. Reasons earn marks.
Use ordinary angle facts too: triangles 180°, straight lines 180°.

example.question: A, B and C are on a circle with centre O. Angle OAB = 20°. Find angle ACB, giving reasons.
steps: OA = OB (radii), so triangle OAB is isosceles: angle OBA = 20°.
Angle AOB = 180° − 20° − 20° = 140° (angles in a triangle add to 180°).
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference.

text: A point C is on a circle with centre O. Angle AOB = 140°. Kim wrote the line below. Find her mistake.
questions.working: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference, so halve it.

m.blurb: No hints. Plan before you calculate.

text: AB is a diameter of a circle with centre O. C is on the circle. The tangent at C meets AB extended at P, and angle CPA = 30°.
questions.working: Angle OCP = 90° (tangent meets radius), so angle COP = 60°. OA = OC (radii), so triangle OAC is isosceles; the exterior angle COP = 2 × angle CAO.

text: Use the angle at the centre theorem to prove that opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°.
questions.answer: Join both opposite vertices to O. The two angles at O are 2a and 2c and make a full turn: 2a + 2c = 360°, so a + c = 180°.

text: In a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, angle A = 2y, angle B = 3x, angle C = 4y − 30° and angle D = x + 40°. Find x and y.
PA and PB are tangents to a circle with centre O, and angle APB = 40°. C is a point on the major arc AB. Find angle ACB, giving reasons.
questions.working: Angle AOB = 360° − 90° − 90° − 40° = 140°. Angle at the centre is twice angle ACB.

text: A circle has radius 13 cm. A chord of the circle is 24 cm long. Find the distance from the centre to the chord.
questions.working: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord: √(13² − 12²).

closed_points: Recognise all seven circle theorems in a diagram.
Write a reason for every angle you find.
Spot the isosceles triangle made by two radii.
Combine theorems with angle facts in multi-step chains.
Prove a circle theorem from another.
